```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(essential8)
```

Use MEPA for the existing individual assessment pathway. DASH and HEI-2015
percentiles support population research and use distinct measurement
instruments. An HEI-2015 total is not itself a percentile or an LE8 diet score.

This extension accepts **already-computed** DASH/HEI indices or percentiles.
Construct dietary indices with an established method appropriate for the
scientific question before supplying them to `score_le8()`. The package's
existing explicit raw-intake calls remain available for compatibility, as
described at the end of this article.

## Already-computed percentiles

Supply percentile points in `diet_value`, on the 0-100 scale. The selected
instrument remains explicit in `diet_method`. Percentiles bypass all
reference lookup, so externally weighted, international, or site-specific
references can be used.

```{r direct}
# Include a second LE8 component to demonstrate a usable composite.
patients <- data.frame(age = c(45, 65), sleep_hours = c(7.5, 7.5),
                       diet_value = c(35, 98))
scores <- suppressWarnings(score_le8(
  patients, diet_method = "dash", min_components = 2
))
scores[c("diet_value", "le8_diet_score", "le8_n_components")]
stopifnot(identical(scores$le8_diet_score, c(25, 100)))
```

The warnings suppressed in these teaching examples identify the other six
unavailable LE8 components. Selecting a population diet method itself does
not produce a warning. Missing diet values propagate to missing scores and
are never imputed. Normal package warnings about entirely unavailable
components remain in effect.

Values such as `0.95` are never multiplied by 100. To catch common proportion
errors, a batch confined to 0-1 with any fractional value is rejected with a
scale message. That heuristic also rejects genuine fractional percentiles
below 1 when they constitute the whole batch; 0 and 1 endpoints alone are
accepted. All other observed values must be finite numeric values in 0-100.

## Already-computed index scores

Supply an index in `dash` or `hei2015`, matching `diet_method`, and select an
explicit reference. The built-in `nhanes_2015_2018` reference is packaged
locally; scoring performs no downloads. Its four derived cutpoints identify
percentile categories. They cannot establish an exact percentile.

```{r built-in}
patients <- data.frame(age = c(45, 65), sleep_hours = c(7.5, 7.5),
                       hei2015 = c(45, 80))
scores <- suppressWarnings(score_le8(
  patients, diet_method = "hei2015", reference = "nhanes_2015_2018",
  min_components = 2
))
scores[c("hei2015", "le8_diet_score")]
```

Use either the index column or `diet_value`, not both, even when the latter
is entirely missing. The generic legacy `diet_method = "percentile"` route
also remains available. MEPA continues to require its original screener
inputs and has no reference-distribution dependency.

## What the built-in reference represents

Both built-in references were derived from public CDC NHANES 2015-2016 and
2017-2018 files and the corresponding USDA FPED releases. They describe
**8,241 nonpregnant adults aged at least 20** with two reliable recalls,
positive energy and two-day dietary weights, and complete required inputs.
Unknown pregnancy status is not treated as known pregnancy.

The builder combines the same two days' constituents and energy before
calculating indices. It divides `WTDR2D` by two to combine the two survey
cycles, nests `SDMVSTRA` within cycle, and specifies `SDMVPSU` in a survey
design. Adult/nonpregnant eligibility is a domain restriction. Weighted
quantiles use `survey::svyquantile(qrule = "math", ci = FALSE)`.

The HEI-2015 reference uses individual scoring of the two-recall mean inputs,
following NCI component standards, units, and legume allocation. It is not an
estimate of the usual-intake distribution or a population-ratio score.
Indices constructed using materially different methods need a suitable
custom reference.

The DASH reference is specifically `essential8_fung_fped_v1`, an eight-component
Fung-style index on the 8-40 scale. Its FPED serving conversions and food-code
definitions are documented in `data-raw/README.md`. They use the numeric food
codes from a pinned revision of the published dietaryindex implementation.
We replace that implementation's unweighted quintiles with pooled weighted
adult quintiles and calculate the index after averaging intakes, rather than
averaging separately scored days. The package's pre-existing lower-quintile
tie convention is retained. Thus **an arbitrary score labeled DASH is not
automatically compatible**, even if it also ranges from 8 to 40. Its reference
must match its index definition and intake quintiles.

These references are independently derived estimates, not published AHA
cutpoint tables or a claim to reproduce a particular published prevalence
estimate exactly. The AHA advisory identifies NHANES 2015-2018 as the initial
reference period; other populations or future methods can use custom
references. The percentile mapping helper is age-independent, but the adult
reference supplied here is not a pediatric reference.

The repository's `data-raw/build_diet_references.R` rebuilds the references.
It records input URLs and SHA-256 hashes, software versions, sample counts,
index definitions, and design details. Only compact derived references and
their provenance are packaged; no participant records or raw downloads are
included. A second build verifies stored cutpoints, sample counts, and source
hashes. CRAN examples and tests never rebuild or download reference data.

## Custom references

Construct method-tagged cutpoints at the 25th, 50th, 75th, and 95th percentiles
of the appropriate index distribution. They must be finite numeric scalars
in nondecreasing order. Repeated values are permitted; equality enters the
higher category, and all tied scores receive the same result.

```{r custom}
# Synthetic teaching values, not an empirical reference.
custom <- diet_reference(
  p25 = 40, p50 = 55, p75 = 65, p95 = 80,
  method = "hei2015", label = "Synthetic study reference",
  source = "Teaching example"
)
custom
scores <- suppressWarnings(score_le8(
  patients, diet_method = "hei2015", reference = custom,
  min_components = 2
))
scores[c("hei2015", "le8_diet_score")]
```

A reference tagged as HEI-2015 cannot be used for DASH, or vice versa.
HEI-2015 is bounded by 0-100. Custom DASH references have no assumed global
index range; use `score_range` when the chosen index has known bounds.
Labels and source metadata do not change scores. References are revalidated
when used, including after an object is modified.

Always name the reference explicitly in published analysis scripts. Adding
or removing patients cannot change other patients' scores. To use your own
cohort intentionally, construct its reference separately and explicitly.

## Compatibility with the existing raw-intake routes

The raw calculations introduced in PR #15 already existed on `dev` when this
extension was written. Existing calls with `dash_columns`/`dash_cutpoints` or
`hei2015_columns`/`hei2015_cutpoints` continue to use their original helpers,
units, outputs, and user-supplied cutpoints. Their matching prefixed raw input
columns are also recognized. See `?score_le8` for the full input contract.

Those explicit compatibility routes bypass the new built-in reference; they
must not be combined with an already-computed index or observed percentile.
No new recall parser, usual-intake model, or index-processing public API is
introduced. Index and percentile calls add no new provenance or component
columns beyond the existing output schema. The 13 detailed HEI components
remain specific to raw-intake compatibility calls.

- [USDA FPED releases](https://www.ars.usda.gov/northeast-area/beltsville-md-bhnrc/beltsville-human-nutrition-research-center/food-surveys-research-group/docs/fped-databases/).

- [NCI HEI scoring standards](https://epi.grants.cancer.gov/hei/developing.html)
